public_rationale: The disclosed cumulative payments imply approximately $728 million of DDTL 1.0 debt service in 2025: $460 million principal plus $268 million interest. This is 27.2% below the forecast's $1 billion and outside the generous approximation band. The quarterly average was $182 million; that average does not establish the payment in any particular quarter.
limitations: This assesses the numerical outcome, not whether the expectation was reasonable when written.
The figures are rounded company disclosures.
Later years and the eventual balloon payment are outside this assessment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: It is not unreasonable to expect that, from this year, CoreWeave will spend around $250m each quarter, or $1bn annually, servicing DDTL 1.0, regardless of the size of the balloon payment.
conditions: regardless of the balloon payment size

statement.excerpt: Still, regardless of the balloon payment size, it’s not unreasonable to expect that, from this year, CoreWeave will be spending around $250m each quarter to service this loan, or $1bn annually.

from_speaker: regardless of the balloon payment size
our_interpretation: This year means calendar 2025, the first year expressly covered by the forecast.
Servicing DDTL 1.0 means cash principal repayments plus cash interest payments on that facility.
The wording expresses an expectation rather than certainty. The reasonableness of the original forecast is distinct from whether its numerical outcome occurred.
For around, use a generous 20% band: $800 million to $1.2 billion annually, with the quarterly figures tested separately if available.
The phrase regardless of the balloon payment size does not create an antecedent that must occur.
criteria.support_condition: Facility-specific disclosures show approximately $1 billion of principal and interest payments during 2025, with approximately $250 million per quarter where quarterly payments are disclosed.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Facility-specific 2025 payments fall materially outside that range. A full-year total below $800 million is sufficient to contradict the annual forecast.
